font.reason: Geometric/techy variable Kufi gives the machine-computing voice SF Mono had; Vazir Code looks stretched on Persian prose. Weight 500, size fs(28)=31 design px so the line keeps the original side margins.

comps.translatedSummary: Title 'TEMPLATE MOTION DEMO' becomes «نمونه نمایشی قالب حرکت» (22 chars, 3 gaps; source prompt wants ~20 so the lock window 24f..82f keeps its density). Noise pool is Persian letters, Persian digits and symbols.

rtlDecisions.what: Lock order (left to right in the original)
rtlDecisions.why: Lock follows reading order; with direction:rtl and characters in logical order the locked prefix grows from the right edge.

Per-char cells force isolated letter forms. Each word keeps an invisible ghost box of the final word that owns the width; live characters are inline spans inside it, so locked letters join like real Persian and the line does not jitter.
Persian letters, Persian digits and #$%&*+= (47 entries kept; <>/\ dropped because bidi mirrors them). Same seeded hash indexing, no Math.random.

rtlDecisions.what: Flash colours, glow, timings, seeds, lockAt formula, 6f blank opening, 96f duration
rtlDecisions.why: Motion fidelity; glow is radial and symmetric. Spaces are never scrambled.
Noto Kufi Arabic 500 at fs(28); line-height FA_LH.

concerns: Noise glyphs are proportional, so during scrambling a word can overhang its ghost box by a little; contained within the frame.
Final lock frame is ~82f; final 14f are a static hold as in the original.
lessons: Scramble/decode per-character effects on Persian: do not use fixed per-letter cells (isolated forms ruin the final read). Use a per-word invisible ghost box for width plus inline per-character spans (colour/text-shadow spans do not break joining in Chromium), with chars in logical order so the lock sweep runs right to left automatically.
